title: Select the minimum sufficient controller for four real loops
equipment: Cold room, recirculating water heater, buffer tank, and loaded positioning table
physicalPurpose: Match controller structure to plant physics, actuator capability, disturbance class, and quantified requirements instead of selecting PID by default.
objective: Select and defend ON/OFF, P, PI, or PID for four different real loops and prove each choice on executable plants.

simplifications: The four loops run together for comparison but do not physically interact.
The tank selection assumes known constant outflow represented by the 20 percent equilibrium bias; an unknown changed outflow is outside this P-control decision.
Structure codes record engineering decisions for this declared worksheet and are not an automatic controller-selection algorithm.

baseline.limitation: PID cannot be realized by the binary compressor and adds unjustified dynamic state or noise sensitivity to loops whose requirements are met by simpler structures.

change.decision: Require every candidate to pass all declared requirements, then choose the eligible structure with the fewest justified dynamic mechanisms.

disturbances: Native comparison applies heater ambient-equivalent bias change from 20 to 17 degC at 60 s

acceptance.window: 100 to 120 s under 4 N m load

abortPredicates: Any signal is nonfinite or outside its hard limit
Compressor output is not exactly 0 or 100 percent
A candidate is accepted after failing a declared requirement
safety.restorationMode: Stop experiment, return every loop to its lesson-specific safe Manual state, and restore initial conditions
safety.physicalApprovalRole: authorised controls engineer for all represented equipment
simulationOnlyRestrictions: The shared four-plant experiment is simulation evidence. Each physical loop requires independent topology, safety, authority, and experiment approval.

video.viewerOutcome: Choose the simplest eligible controller for a binary thermal loop, self-regulating thermal loop, integrating inventory loop, and loaded motion loop.

learning.context: Four common loops have different actuator capabilities, plant dynamics, disturbances, and performance requirements.
learning.reason: The learner knows each controller structure but needs to select from evidence rather than always applying the most complex one.
theory: A candidate is eligible only if it satisfies every accuracy, dynamic, actuator, disturbance, noise, and safety requirement with margin.
The minimum sufficient controller is the eligible structure with the fewest justified dynamic mechanisms and retained states.

Binary actuation favors protected ON/OFF control; a self-regulating process needing zero load offset commonly needs PI; an integrating plant can supply setpoint integration; a loaded oscillatory motion plant can require PID.
Every selection is conditional on the declared requirement and operating boundary. A changed disturbance or actuator can change the correct structure.
learning.workedPrediction: The cold room cycles at 1.5/2.5 degC with 5 s dwell. The heater needs 50 percent at 30 degC. The tank's P closed-loop time constant is 2.5 s around 20 percent bias. PD on the loaded table predicts approximately 0.316 rad equilibrium error, while PID can retain 4 N m at zero error.
practicalPreparation: Write each controlled-variable, actuator, setpoint, disturbance, accuracy, dynamic, noise, constraint, and safety requirement before selecting a structure.
In Control Studio verify all four SP/PV/MV sets, selected codes, enabled terms, limits, state, quality, event timing, and simulation label.
learning.baseline: Apply the rejected rule 'PID everywhere' and identify the actuator mismatch or unnecessary mechanisms before running it.
learning.change: Run ON/OFF, PI, biased P, and PID on the four executable plants under their declared events, then change one worksheet requirement at a time without silently changing the plant.
learning.comparison: Compare requirement coverage first. Use mechanism and retained-state count only to choose among candidates that passed every requirement.
learning.validation: Require protected cold-room cycling, heater error at most 0.10 degC after the load event, tank error at most 0.05 cm, table error at most 0.02 rad, and no limit or validity violation.
learning.explanation: The selected structures differ because the physical plants and required outcomes differ. Feature count is not control quality.
learning.transfer: Use the worksheet on unfamiliar loops only after classifying their response. Lesson 32 teaches those plant response classes.
